question: The Commission has approved the acquisition by the Chinese company JD.com of approximately 58 % of the shares in the German Ceconomy group, which owns the MediaMarkt and Saturn chains, and thus the acquisition of a majority stake in the company. Publicly available information indicates that JD.com has benefited from Chinese state support, including loans on preferential terms, tax breaks and subsidies.

Such subsidies may result in a distortion of competition on the EU’s internal market and are subject to specific scrutiny under EU law. According to media reports, the Commission’s approval of the transaction was made conditional on JD.com undertaking not to pass on any unauthorised financial support to the acquired company that could distort competition on the EU market. In light of the above: 1.

When analysing the transaction, did the Commission take into account not only potential threats to competition on the internal market, but also possible risks to the security of the EU and its citizens, in particular with regard to the protection of personal data and information security?

On what grounds did the Commission ultimately approve the transaction, despite earlier concerns raised by Commission representatives regarding the acquisition of the German group by a Chinese company?

How does the Commission intend to monitor and enforce JD.com’s compliance with its commitment not to provide unauthorised financial support to the acquired company, and have specific monitoring mechanisms, reporting obligations and sanctions in the event of a breach of these commitments been put in place?
